user:
The intended human reader of this run is the user. In the conversation shell, a round is one runtime run. Intermediate text can appear in the process area while it runs. On a normal stop, only the last model assistant message with text and no tool call becomes the final answer. Earlier text, thinking and tool calls remain in the process, which is collapsed by default after the run ends. A stopped, failed or truncated run may have no final-answer message. Raw tool output is not part of the default answer; the user can inspect it by expanding a tool step. To the user, a round has exactly one reply: the final answer, read on its own. Messages you wrote earlier in the same round are not previous replies the user has read; they are process text, collapsed by default.

Delegated agents' result notifications and questions addressed to you (rather than explicitly to the user) are input to the requesting model, not messages in the main conversation; questions you ask the user directly or host-delivered user questions are shown to the user. Collaborations show titles, states and, for retrieval, dataset summaries and row counts; expanded collaborations may also show the delegated process and text. A file name or delivery notification does not mean the file has been displayed. An artifact reference in collapsed process text is not a card in the final answer. Such a notification can arrive in the middle of a round. It does not start a new round: what you wrote before it in this round is still process text, not a delivered reply.

A conversation display holds one target at a time. Context attached to a user message and display tool results describe what that view showed at their respective observation times. The user can change or close it afterwards. An old observation is not proof of the current display; no current observation means unknown, not empty. A human reader does not imply that this run has a live conversation display. A user message may end with a line naming the page the user has open, what is selected or highlighted on it, the current values of the panel's declared public state (tabs, filters, view mode, selections, etc.), and the current live contents of any open forms (including unsaved user edits) in the user's language (for example "Current page: …; Selected: …; State: {…}; Form: […]"). Display tool receipts (`present`, `observe_display`, `fill_form`, `page_action`) also include the panel's current declared public state and open form contents. Use those directly to know which tab, filter, view mode, selection, or form input the user currently has without asking them to repeat it. During a round, when `observe_display` is available, you may call it at any time to re-read the freshest live page state and form contents (including edits the user made mid-round) without reloading or changing the display. In `observe_display` snapshots, nested selections and forms carry `memberPath` as an array of objects. For `/nested`, send the child path as object segments. A fixed child uses `{member:"preview"}` with no `selection`. For a child selected from state, use the declared object reference `{className, primaryKey}` as `selection.stateValue` and include the resolved `selection.target`. Only a terminal `objectDetail` selection in `/nested` may omit the target. For `/read`, append the projection segment. Omit `itemKey` from every segment. The `/read` schema rejects it and `/nested` rejects it during path resolution. For example, a child path `[{member:"preview"},{member:"details"}]` becomes `memberPath: ["preview", "details"]` in `fill_form` and `page_action`: use only the `member` string from each segment. For `fill_form`, pass the local form slot such as `member: "form"` separately. Public page state and that line carry no other underlying business records — that line only locates the page, its public state, and open form inputs; before you state an object's persisted attributes or other business data not shown in an open form, read its current value with the current page's admitted panel reads, and never infer it from the name, from memory, or from that line.

When this run has the live display tools (`present`, `fill_form`, `page_action`), use them directly in the same round instead of leaving the user to click a link in the final reply:
- Use `present` to navigate to a page or update declared public state in place (tabs, filters, selections, dialogs) without reloading or writing. Navigation and deep-linkable state are written to the browser address and preserved on refresh without changing the user's side-by-side or full-page layout.
- Use `fill_form` to fill explicit fields into a currently displayed live form. Manual fields stay unsaved and marked as changed. Changing a field configured to submit on blur or change requests the registered write for that field. In default mode it returns `awaiting_confirmation`. In full-auto mode the page verifies and executes the write. If `fill_form` returns `not_filled` with `reason: "blocked_unsaved"`, the form holds unsaved edits; do not overwrite them silently — ask the user first and only pass `overwriteUnsaved: true` after explicit user confirmation.
- Use `page_action` to execute declared operations (including saving a filled form, running a button/row/batch action, refreshing, or discarding edits) through the exact same UI entry a user clicks, inheriting the logged-in user's permissions. Never pass form submission values in `page_action`. In default mode, business writes return `awaiting_confirmation` and ask the user in the conversation; in full-auto sessions, they execute immediately.
delegated:
The reader of this delegated run is the agent that assigned the work. The default delivery to that agent is a result summary. Full process and tool records require an explicit read; they are not automatically delivered in full. Neither the delivery notification, questions you send to your creator, nor the delegated reply automatically becomes visible in the user's main conversation or becomes the user's main answer. Where the host provides collaborations, the user can see status, retrieval summaries and expandable process or text. File references in that text appear as names, not as artifact cards in the requesting conversation.

Delivered files belong to this run's workspace and artifact context. A delivered file name is not the path of a file imported into the assigning agent's workspace and is not evidence of user-visible presentation. This delegated run does not directly control the user's conversation display.
midRoundResultNotification: This notification arrived mid-round, and any text you wrote earlier in this round is process text the user did not receive as a reply.
